title: Finite-level bounded constructibility for proper support
statement:
Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be
finite-type $K_0$-schemes, and let
$f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
$K_0$-morphism. Fix a prime $\ell$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and
require that its image in $K_0$ is invertible. Choose a finite extension
$E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$,
and put $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $Rf_{!,n}$ be the coherent finite-level
compact-support direct image
functor associated to the
compactification candidates.
The comparison maps are identities for identity refinements and satisfy the cocycle
condition, and $D^b_c(X,A)$ uses
finite-torsion
constructibility. For $a,b\in\mathbf Z$ with $a\leq b$, write

$$
D_c^{[a,b]}(X,A)=\{K\in D^b_c(X,A):
\mathcal H^r(K)=0\text{ for }r\notin[a,b]\},
$$

where $D^b_c(X,A)$ has the
finite-torsion
constructibility condition, and $\mathcal H^r$ is the
cohomology-sheaf functor.
The ambient
derived direct-image functor
$Rf_{!,n}$ restricts to an exact triangulated functor

$$
Rf_{!,n}:D^b_c(X,A_{E,n})
\longrightarrow D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n}).
$$

For each cohomological interval
$[a,b]$ with $a,b\in\mathbf Z$ and
$a\leq b$, and each integer $e\geq0$ such that every
geometric fiber of $f$ has
dimension at most $e$, there
are integers $a'\leq b'$, independent of the compactification, such that
for every $K\in D_c^{[a,b]}(X,A_{E,n})$ one has

$$
Rf_{!,n}K\in D_c^{[a',b']}(Y,A_{E,n}).
$$

Finite coefficient reduction is interpreted on its bounded domain: for $1\leq m\leq n$, put $B=A_{E,m}$ and $K_m=K\otimes_A^L B$, using ordinary derived extension of scalars. Whenever $K\in D^b_c(X,A)$ and $K_m\in D^b_c(X,B)$, the canonical coefficient comparison is an isomorphism
$$
 (Rf_{!,n}K)\otimes_A^L B\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,m}K_m
$$
in $D^b_c(Y,B)$. For any $e\geq0$ bounding the dimensions of all geometric fibres of $f$, if $K_m$ has cohomology in $[c,d]$, its direct image has cohomology in $[c,d+2e]$, with the same bound independent of the compactification and of $m$. No assertion that derived reduction preserves boundedness or the original cohomological interval of every bounded constructible $A$-complex is intended.
(*Sources: Stacks Project, Tag `0GL0` (`more-etale.tex`, `theorem-constructible-shriek`), for compact-support constructibility; Tag `095U` (`etale-cohomology.tex`, `lemma-cohomological-dimension-proper`), for the proper fibre-dimension estimate underlying the finite-type compact-support bound; and Tag `0GL6` (`more-etale.tex`, `remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings`), for coefficient compatibility.*)

proof.text: Coefficient and compactification setup. The finite coefficient datum [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] gives $A=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$ finite. It is annihilated by a power of $\ell$: write $\ell=u\varpi_E^r$ with $r>0$ in the valuation ring, and take a power with exponent $s$ satisfying $sr\geq n$. Thus the annihilator is invertible over $K_0$. Choose the compactification already used to define the functor, $c=(j,p)$ with $f=pj$. Its candidate is exactly $Rp_*j_!$ by [def-weil-compact-support-candidate], and [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] specifies the coherent functor on the étale-origin domain. The properness definition [def-weil-proper-morphism] makes $p$ finite type. To check that $\overline X$ is finite type over $K_0$, use [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]: take a finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ of $Y$ with each $R_i$ finitely generated over $K_0$, and a finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}S_{it}$ of each inverse image under $p$, with $S_{it}$ finitely generated over $R_i$. The images of generators for $R_i$ together with generators for $S_{it}$ generate $S_{it}$ over $K_0$. A field is Noetherian since it has only two ideals, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X,Y,\overline X$ Noetherian. In particular each has a finite affine cover by Noetherian rings: choose Noetherian affine neighbourhoods by local Noetherianity, then a finite subcover by quasi-compactness. We prove the assertions for this candidate. Once the input is shown to have étale origin in Step 2, [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] identifies the candidates for all compactifications, naturally with identity and cocycle laws. We do not infer any dimension bound for the boundary of this arbitrary compactification.

source.place: Step 1, with the domain restriction in the compact-support definition

proof.text:
Descend the bounded input to the étale site. Apply clause (ii) of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] to obtain $G\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and a witness $
u_X^*G\cong K$. This interface quantifies over every scheme $T$; its auxiliary finite-field datum can be chosen of any characteristic different from $\ell$, and imposes no structure map from $X$ or $Y$ to that field. Its intrinsic finite-stratification condition is exactly [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. By [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], $\mathcal H^r(
u_X^*G)=
u_X^*\mathcal H^r(G)$. The sheaf unit is an isomorphism by [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level], so $
u_X^*$ reflects zero sheaves. Consequently $G$ has the same cohomological interval $[a,b]$ as $K$. For the chosen compactification, [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] now gives the natural isomorphism $Rf_{!,n}K\cong
u_Y^*(Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}j^{\mathrm{et}}_!G)$. This cited comparison includes the open-extension comparison as well as the proper direct-image comparison; a direct-image comparison alone would not suffice.

source.place: Step 2, with Stacks Tags 09AK and 09AL (intrinsic constructibility versus étale origin)

proof.text: Bounded constructibility by the proper factor. Exactness of étale extension by zero is [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]. Applying it termwise gives $\mathcal H^r(j_!^{\mathrm{et}}G)=j_!^{\mathrm{et}}\mathcal H^r(G)$: exactness preserves the kernels and images defining cohomology. Each of these sheaves is constructible by [lem-fin-extension-by-zero], and the zero cohomology sheaves remain zero. Thus $j_!^{\mathrm{et}}G$ is bounded constructible. The chosen $p$ is proper between finite-type $K_0$-schemes, so [lem-fin-proper-bounded-constructible] gives $Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}j_!^{\mathrm{et}}G\in D^b_c(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. The comparison of Step 2 and the constructible-origin equivalence of Step 2 therefore put $Rf_{!,n}K$ in the intrinsic $D^b_c(Y,A)$. This uses no assertion that the geometric fibres of $p$ have the same dimension bound as those of $f$.

source.place: Step 3; Stacks Tag 0GL0 (more-etale.tex, theorem-constructible-shriek), applied in the proper case

proof.text: Sheaf amplitude. The chosen compactification and the Noetherian hypotheses verified in Step 1 allow [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] to identify $Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}j_!^{\mathrm{et}}$ with the compactification-independent étale $Rf_!$ on bounded-below inputs. For a constructible étale $A$-sheaf $F$, [sbc-thm-finiteness-finite-type] applies directly to $f$, and gives $R^qf_!F=0$ for $q>2e$. Negative cohomology vanishes as well: $j_!F$ is a sheaf in degree zero by exactness from Step 3; the category of étale $A$-module sheaves has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Choose an injective resolution in degrees $\geq0$ using [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero]. It is K-injective by [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist], hence computes $Rp_*$ by the K-injective construction in [def-kun-projection-formula-map]; its termwise direct image has no negative terms. The comparison and exact pullback in Step 2 give the interval $[0,2e]$ for $Rf_{!,n}$ on every intrinsic constructible pro-étale sheaf.

source.place: Steps 3–4, sheaf bound for f itself

proof.text: Pass from sheaves to bounded complexes using [lem-pur-bounded-heart-amplitude]. Take $T=Rf_{!,n}^c$, which is triangulated by [lem-compact-support-direct-image-triangulated], and let $\mathcal S$ be the class of intrinsic constructible pro-etale $A$-sheaves, including zero and all its isomorphic copies. Step 4 gives the lemma's hypothesis with $c=0,d=2e$. Each $H^r(K)$ is in this class and vanishes outside $[a,b]$ by the input condition. Thus $Rf_{!,n}^cK$ has interval $[a,b+2e]$. Its bounded constructibility was proved in Step 3. Take $a'=a$, $b'=b+2e$; these depend only on $a,b,e$, and Step 1 identifies all compactification candidates on this input.

source.place: Steps 3–4, finite cohomology induction now factored through a generic amplitude lemma

proof.text: Restriction as a triangulated functor. Step 3 proves that the ambient functor maps the full bounded constructible subcategory into the corresponding full subcategory on $Y$. It preserves shifts and distinguished triangles by [lem-compact-support-direct-image-triangulated]. The triangulated structures on the full subcategories in [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] are the induced ones, so this same functor and the same shift comparison restrict, giving the asserted exact triangulated functor. Step 1 transports this restriction between compactifications.

Coefficient reduction and the underlying A-linear comparison. Fix $B=A_{E,m}$ and an etale input $G$ from Step 2 whose actual reduction $G_B=G\otimes_A^LB$ is bounded constructible; Step 10 will verify this from the hypothesis on $K_m$. Write $J=j_!^AG$. Derived scalar extension is [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]; its underlying $A$-complex is tensor with $B$, by [lem-pur-change-of-rings-tensor-comparison] applied to a K-flat resolution. Properness of $p$ and torsion of $A$ allow [lem-kun-0f0g], with coefficient complex $B_Y[0]$, without a finite-Tor assumption on $B$. Follow its projection isomorphism with [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor] to obtain
$$(Rp_{*,A}j_!^AG)\otimes_A^LB\cong Rp_{*,A}j_!^A(\operatorname{Res}G_B)$$
as $A$-complexes. Restriction of scalars leaves finite stalks and locally constant strata unchanged, so $\operatorname{Res}G_B$ is bounded constructible over $A$. Step 3 makes the displayed right side bounded, hence the left side bounded. Forgetting scalar action leaves cohomology unchanged, so $L_B(Rp_{*,A}J)$ is bounded as a $B$-complex as well.

source.place: Step 5; Stacks Tags 0F0G, 0GL1 and 0GL6, first the A-linear projection isomorphism

proof.text: The open comparison has its B-action. Choose a K-flat resolution $P\to G$ as in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For every acyclic $A$-complex $C$, the sheaf tensor identity of [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor] identifies the total complex $(j_!P)\otimes_A C$ with $j_!(P\otimes_A j^{-1}C)$. Exactness of inverse image [def-kun-projection-formula-map] makes $j^{-1}C$ acyclic, so K-flatness of $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] and exactness of $j_!$ [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] make this total complex acyclic. Thus $j_!P$ is K-flat. The degreewise identity $(j_!P)\otimes_A B\cong j_!^B(P\otimes_A B)$ is B-linear, with B acting on the same tensor factor on both sides. It computes the natural B-linear isomorphism $L_BJ\cong j_!^BG_B$; after forgetting B it is the open tensor comparison used in Step 7.

source.place: Step 5; Stacks 0GL1 and 0E8I, explicit K-flat test and degreewise B-action

proof.text: Identify the proper coefficient morphism, rather than selecting an A-linear isomorphism. Apply [lem-pur-etale-scalar-mate-projection] to $p$ and $J=j_!^AG$. Here $J$ is bounded by Step 3, its B-reduction is bounded by Step 8 and boundedness of $G_B$, and $L_B(Rp_{*,A}J)$ is bounded by Step 7. The lemma gives the canonical B-linear counit-transpose map to $Rp_{*,B}L_BJ$ and identifies its restriction with the projection-formula map of Step 7, under the canonical restriction/direct-image comparison. Compose with the B-linear open isomorphism of Step 8. The restricted composite is precisely the isomorphism displayed in Step 7. Restriction detects isomorphisms because its cohomology is the same underlying sheaf of abelian groups; a map is a quasi-isomorphism for one scalar action exactly when it is for the other. Hence this specified B-linear coefficient comparison is an isomorphism.

source.place: Step 5; Stacks 0GL6, the canonical proper scalar mate identified with the projection map

proof.text: Transport reduction and its bound to the pro-étale site, keeping the bounded domain explicit. Comparison pullback is exact and commutes with cohomology by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. Its canonical derived tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], computed on K-flat resolutions and with $\nu^{-1}B_X=B_X$, identifies $\nu_X^*(G\otimes_A^LB)$ with $K_m=K\otimes_A^LB$ as $B$-complexes. If $K_m$ is bounded constructible, then so is $G\otimes_A^LB$: the sheaf unit of [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] reflects vanishing; full faithfulness of the same sheaf pullback, combined with clause (i) of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], reflects constructibility degree by degree. Explicitly, descend a constructible pullback to a constructible étale sheaf, then full faithfulness lifts the isomorphism back to the original cohomology sheaf. Thus both inputs to [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] at $A$ and $B$ are bounded below. Apply its canonical comparisons, the tensor comparison on $Y$, and Steps 7–9 to obtain the stated coefficient isomorphism in $D^b_c(Y,B)$. Its sources and targets are bounded constructible because the target is so by Step 3 at $B$, and it is an isomorphism. Under restriction of scalars the $B$-candidate is identified with the $A$-candidate by [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]; this also specifies which coefficient functors are being compared. Applying Step 5 at $B$ to the interval $[c,d]$ of $K_m$ gives $[c,d+2e]$. The same calculation works for every $m$ and every compactification. It does not assert that $K_m$ has the original interval $[a,b]$, or is bounded for every $K$.

source.place: Step 5, finite reduction, with Stacks Tag 0GL6 and the exact site/tensor comparison

proof_origin.place: Steps 1–5, with the proper projection/open tensor argument of Stacks Tags 0F0G, 0GL1 and 0GL6 for reduction

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be
finite-type $K_0$-schemes, and let
$f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
$K_0$-morphism. Fix a prime $\ell$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and
require that its image in $K_0$ is invertible. Choose a finite extension
$E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$,
and put $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $Rf_{!,n}$ be the coherent finite-level
compact-support direct image
functor associated to the
compactification candidates.
The comparison maps for refinements are identities and satisfy the cocycle
condition, and $D^b_c(X,A)$ uses
finite-torsion
constructibility. For $a,b\in\mathbf Z$ with $a\leq b$, write

$$
D_c^{[a,b]}(X,A)=\{K\in D^b_c(X,A):
\mathcal H^r(K)=0\text{ for }r\notin[a,b]\},
$$

where $D^b_c(X,A)$ has the
finite-torsion
constructibility condition, and $\mathcal H^r$ is the
cohomology-sheaf functor.
The ambient
derived direct-image functor
$Rf_{!,n}$ restricts to an exact triangulated functor

$$
Rf_{!,n}:D^b_c(X,A_{E,n})
\longrightarrow D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n}).
$$

For each cohomological interval
$[a,b]$ with $a,b\in\mathbf Z$ and
$a\leq b$, and each integer $e\geq0$ such that every
geometric fiber of $f$ has
dimension at most $e$, there
are integers $a'\leq b'$, independent of the compactification, such that
for every $K\in D_c^{[a,b]}(X,A_{E,n})$ one has

$$
Rf_{!,n}K\in D_c^{[a',b']}(Y,A_{E,n}).
$$

The restriction and its amplitude bound commute with finite coefficient
reduction.

proof.text:
*Step 1 (the compactification form).* By
[def-weil-compact-support-candidate] a compactification of $f$
is a factorisation $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$
an open immersion ([def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]) and
$\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper ([def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]),
and the candidate
attached to it is $R\bar f_*\circ j_!$, formed with the
derived direct image ([def-weil-derived-direct-image]); the functor
$Rf_{!,n}$ of
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] is the coherent choice of a
candidate in the compactification category
[def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and by the hypothesis
recalled in the statement its comparison maps are identities satisfying
the cocycle condition. It therefore suffices to bound the candidate of
a single compactification, and the bound produced below involves only
the amplitude interval of $K$ and the fibre bound $e$, so that it is
independent of the choice.

*Step 2 (transport to the étale site).* The functor is defined on
the pro-étale categories. Under the comparison morphism of sites
$\nu$ of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] the direct images
correspond, $\nu^*Ru_{{\mathrm{et}},*}\cong Ru_{{\mathrm{proet}},*}\nu^*$
([prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image]), and constructibility on
the pro-étale site is by definition the inverse image of
constructibility on the étale site
([def-weil-pbc-constructible-direct-image-finiteness]). It is
accordingly enough to prove the assertion for the étale direct image,
which is what the two classical finiteness theorems below provide.

*Step 3 (extension by zero and the proper case).* For
$K\in D^b_c(X,A)$ the object $j_!K$ lies in $D^b_c(\bar X,A)$ with
constructible cohomology
sheaves ([def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]) in the same degrees: extension by zero
is exact and preserves
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]
([def-weil-extension-by-zero], [lem-fin-extension-by-zero]).
The geometric fibres of $\bar f$ have dimension at most $e$, so
[obl-fin-comparison] applies to $\bar f$: for every constructible
$A$-sheaf $F$ on $\bar X_{{\mathrm{et}}}$ the sheaves
$R^q\bar f_*F$ are constructible and vanish for $q>2e$. For a
complex whose cohomology sheaves lie in degrees $[a,b]$ the conclusion
holds degreewise, the constructible sheaves forming a weak Serre
subcategory ([thm-constructible-serre]), so that
$Rf_{!,n}K\in D_c^{[a,b+2e]}(Y,A)$ for the
constructible cohomological
interval ([def-weil-constructible-intervals]) $D_c^{[a,b+2e]}(Y,A)$.

*Step 4 (the finite-type form).* The same bound is available
without compactifying. By [sbc-thm-finiteness-finite-type],
applied to the finite-type morphism $f$ over the field $K_0$ whose
geometric fibres have dimension at most $e$, the sheaves $R^qf_!F$
are constructible for every $q$ and vanish for $q>2e$, for every
constructible $A$-sheaf $F$; the case of a complex follows as in
Step 3.

*Step 5 (exactness and reduction).* The restriction is a
triangulated functor, $j_!$ and $R\bar f_*$ being exact and
triangulated on the bounded constructible categories, and it commutes
